independent.summary: The site-wide strip runs inside keepPara, so it removes footer hours blocks before buildHoursChunk (LEO-018) ever sees them: chunkText builds allParas with keepPara(p, cs) and passes that list to buildHoursChunk, so a 'Monday - Saturday / 7 am - 2 pm' footer repeated on >=40% of pages is gone from every page's paragraph list and no dedicated '[H2] Hours' chunk is produced on any crawl after the first (including force scrapes, which also pass the cached fingerprints). The text survives only inside the mixed 1700-char 'Site-wide info' chunk — exactly the low-scoring mixed-chunk situation LEO-018 measured at 0.68 vs 0.79 — so the repo's top known issue ('RAG misses what are your hours?') is re-opened, and no test covers the interaction (the fixture FOOTER is a single >80-char line, which buildHoursChunk skips).

In rescrapeSite thin-page detection uses estimateContentLen(text), which calls keepPara WITHOUT cs and therefore does not strip site-wide chrome, while embedPageData filters with keepPara(p, cs). A page whose own content is under 300 chars once chrome is stripped (a staff card with name/title/email — the 0a0ab27 case the item forbids regressing) is classified non-thin, goes into changedPages, is pushed onto embedPageData's thinPageData (which rescrapeSite discards — only normalChunks is destructured), and is excluded from allThinPages (same cs-blind measure), so it lands in no group chunk. persistRescrapeResult then sees chunks.length === 0 for a URL in pageHashUpdates and calls clearChunksForUrl, deleting its stored chunks while writing the new contentHash — so the page is silently removed from the corpus and, being 'unchanged' from then on, is never rebuilt. The full-scrape path is consistent (both measures are cs-aware) and does not have the bug.

Stripping only happens when a page is re-chunked, but a smart rescrape re-embeds only changed, priority or stale pages (staleDays defaults to 0 = disabled), so the boilerplate stays in the stored chunks of every unchanged page forever. The measured case the item is about — the reCAPTCHA notice in 139 harvestlanefarmmarket.com chunks — is not cleaned by any number of LeoRefresh runs; only a superadmin force scrape clears it (and that path then loses the hours chunk, see the first finding). The header's claim that a crawl 'converges on the next refresh' and the item's 'strip them from every chunk' are both unmet for existing corpora, and nothing backfills.

Every detected fingerprint is stripped from every page, but the preserved copy is capped: buildSiteWideContent ranks by infoScore and keeps only MAX_BLOCKS=25 blocks under MAX_CHUNK_LEN=1700, so any block beyond the cap is removed from all chunks and stored nowhere — contradicting the header's 'a stripped block is never destroyed'. This bites hardest on exactly the text the old rule protected: eligible() has no upper length bound, so repeated prose over BOILERPLATE_MAX (a mission statement or long footer blurb that previously always passed dedup) is now stripped site-wide and, having an infoScore of 0, is the first thing the length budget drops. The same loop also admits a single oversized first block unconditionally (the `&& kept.length > 0` guard), so the 'stays a chunk, not a page dump' cap is not actually enforced for one block.

chromeUpdate overwrites siteChrome.fingerprints whenever report() returns an array, and report() returns [] whenever pageCount < MIN_SITE_PAGES or nothing clears the floor. A degraded crawl (most fetches failing, robots blocking, a partially reachable site) therefore wipes a good cached fingerprint set, so the next crawl strips nothing and re-admits chrome into every page it re-embeds; the blocks list and pageCount are clobbered with it. Nothing distinguishes 'measured no chrome' from 'did not measure enough pages to tell'.

The 'Site-wide info' write sits outside the snapshot: createSnapshot is called with [...changedUrls, ...thinGroupUrls, ...retiredUrls], which never contains the synthetic /#site-wide URL, so replaceChunksForUrl deletes the previous site-wide chunk without archiving it, and the block runs even on a no-change rescrape where snapshot is null. Every other destructive chunk write in this file is preceded by an archive that makes a restore possible; this one has no restore path.

triageGrades.reason: No auth, role or middleware code is touched; the new route lines sit inside the existing requireAuth()-protected handler.
The only new config is BOILERPLATE_LOG_LEVEL, a log-verbosity string with a default — no credentials or key handling.
No billing, quota, Stripe or pricing code is involved.

Correct that the change touches destructive paths — it adds replaceChunksForUrl for the new synthetic URL and changes which paragraphs survive into (and which stored chunks get cleared by) the persist loop — even though the cited line 230 is an unchanged ScrapedPage bulkWrite.
Wrong: cachedStructure gates the Pass-1 Haiku (Anthropic) call so it may be skipped entirely, and siteWideChunk adds a new Voyage embedTexts call per crawl.
No deploy, version, migration or build config changes; the new Entity subdocument is additive with defaults and the new env var is optional.

summary: The local review found nothing and missed everything, including two serious defects — the destruction of the dedicated hours chunk and a rescrape path that deletes a thin page's chunks without regrouping it — and its only non-trivial triage call (externalApi) is wrong.
